thread:
derek: Noticed a spike of SCIM 403s starting ~02:05 UTC after a scheduled IdP cert rotation. Affected service account: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-provisioner. Logs show mixed KMS errors and a surprising iam:PassRole denial in the same window. Snippet:
```
2026-08-12T02:05:12Z scim-provisioner err="KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied" token=tok-42 user=felix@example.com
2026-08-12T02:05:13Z scim-provisioner http 403 PATCH /Users/424 -> {"error":"forbidden"}
2026-08-12T02:05:14Z aws-iam auth err="AccessDenied: iam:PassRole denied for arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/scim-provisioner" action=UpdateServiceAccount
```
Can someone pick this up? @lia-security @ops-lead

lia-security: on it. First pass: check CloudTrail for PutKeyPolicy, CreateGrant, ReEncrypt, UpdateAssumeRolePolicy, and any iam:PutRolePolicy events in the 02:03-02:07 window. Also confirm whether CloudTrail ingestion to the security account was delayed — we had a gap last month.

ops-lead: mitigation priorities: 1) avoid immediate user deprovisions (increase SCIM grace to 96h and pause prune), 2) restore KMS decrypt capability, 3) restore iam:PassRole semantics if misapplied. Derek, can you widen the grace window and hold prune jobs?

derek: widened grace and paused prune via helm patch. Running CloudTrail queries now. Found PutKeyPolicy at 02:04:59 by infra-automation and an inline role policy UpdateRolePolicy at 02:04:58 that added a deny on iam:PassRole for cross-account principals. Also saw CreateGrant at 02:04:56 that subsequently expired due to a misconfigured GrantTokens param.

jack: interesting — we rely on two mechanisms: a key policy allowing the role and a short-lived KMS grant for performance. If the grant expired unexpectedly and the key policy no longer allowed the role (policy hardening), decrypts would fail. The iam:PassRole deny explains background jobs that attempted to refresh grants failing. Root cause seems to be automation that both rotated the cert and ran a policy-hardening stage which: A) replaced key policy (removed role), B) tightened IAM inline policy (deny iam:PassRole), and C) tried to create ephemeral grant but passed wrong GrantTokens so it wasn't usable.

lia-security: that's consistent with CloudTrail. Also noticed CloudTrail log delivery to our security account lagged by ~6 minutes, so the alerting pipeline didn't page in time. Add that to the post-incident actions. Immediate fix: 1) put back previous key policy that explicitly allows scim-provisioner kms:Decrypt, 2) revert the iam inline deny on iam:PassRole, 3) re-create a valid grant if we still want ephemeral grants, or remove ephemeral grants from pipeline to avoid single-point expiry.

ops-lead: Derek / Jack — who can patch key policy and role policy now? We should also block infra-automation job until gated.

derek: patching key policy now and reverting role inline policy. Commands used: 
```bash
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/scim-provisioner --policy file://allow-scim-provisioner.json
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name scim-provisioner --policy-name allow-passrole --policy-document file://allow-passrole.json
```
Applying a short-lived grant instead of relying on ephemeral token dance removed for now. Restarting scim-provisioner after updating secrets.

infra-automation: [AUDIT] policy-hardening job paused by ops-lead at 2026-08-12T02:10:30Z pending gating changes. PutKeyPolicy id=pkp-1337 created at 02:04:59Z by infra-automation (rolled back).

jack: after restart I'm seeing KMS decrypt succeed and SCIM returning 200s. Example: 
```
2026-08-12T02:11:42Z scim-provisioner http 200 PATCH /Users/424 user=felix@example.com action=update
```
We should watch for role flapping and any remaining reconciliation work for users deprovisioned during the window.

lia-security: post-incident action items (short): - require infra-automation PRs that change KMS key policies or IAM role policies to include a security reviewer and a checklist to preserve runtime principals; - add a CloudTrail diff alert that pages security when a PutKeyPolicy removes known runtime principals; - add a CI preflight that validates `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` for essential operations post-change; - create graceful fallback in SCIM with a list of trusted fallback principals/aliases; - fix CloudTrail delivery lag to security account. Classify the automation as high-risk for vuln triage (config drift impacting availability).

ops-lead: assign owners: @jack add re-encrypt and grant-safe helpers to runbook, @lia-security own gating + alerting, @derek run reconciliation job and draft postmortem, @infra-automation remove ephemeral grant logic and add preflight. ETA EOD.

sre-bot: [INCIDENT] service=scim-provisioner incident=INC-2026-0812-14 status=mitigated mitigated_by=derek mitigated_at=2026-08-12T02:12:35Z runbook=https://redwood.runbooks/internal/scim-provisioning-triage :white_check_mark:

derek: final status — provisioner healthy, no 403s for 20m, audit log attached to postmortem draft. We'll run the reconciliation and close once sanity checks pass. Thanks all. (reactions: :thumbsup: from jack, :eyes: from lia-security)
